ranking.explanation: Keep the earliest feasible arrival. At the same arrival, prefer complete footprints with the largest smallest threshold margin (hours). Break ties by darkness, Earth-gap, and joint-time margins, then center metrics and site ID. All components remain visible; this is a declared preference, not a universal optimum.

worstCase.interpretation: Worst values among supplied discrete positions. Positive margins are hours inside each threshold; negative margins miss it. The minimum is the smallest of the three explicitly reported margins, not a weighted score, probability, or calibrated uncertainty.

interpretation: This reproduces the released 30-minute model. Five-minute independent-position queries are a separate M04 audit.
The nine positions include the center. Their passing count is not an area fraction or landing-success probability.
Angular increments are deterministic stress conditions, not calibrated terrain-error estimates.
All three margins are reported in hours. Minimum margin is the smallest reported slack, not a weighted score. The preference order is explicit and preserves earliest feasible arrival.
Unknown samples do not acquire a whole-footprint worst-case claim; partial known-subset extrema remain separately labeled.
